analysis.title: Aeva Technologies Inc. (AEVA): Progress on optical portfolio, award traction and product ramps in focus; 3Q26 wrap
key_insights: Aeva reported 3Q26 revenue of $6.7 mn versus GS at $6.5 mn and the Street (FactSet) at $6.6 mn. Revenue rose 86.3% y/y and 8.7% q/q.
Adjusted EBIT ex-SBC was -$27.7 mn versus GS at -$26.6 mn and the Street at -$33.4 mn. Non-GAAP EPS ex-SBC was -$0.39 versus GS at -$0.39 and the Street at -$0.43.
GS estimates non-GAAP EPS including SBC at -$0.56 versus its own forecast of -$0.51. 3Q26 free cash flow was -$30.6 mn.
Total liquidity was $272.5 mn at the end of 3Q, made up of $147.5 mn in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities and a $125.0 mn standby preferred equity facility.

First revenue from Optical Connectivity came in the quarter, from deliveries of ultra-high power (UHP) chipsets to its JDA customer for integration and validation. The JDA with an optical engine provider integrates Aeva's high-power optical sources for a hyperscale customer.

Management expects the hyperscaler opportunity, which covers a portion of the hyperscaler's total business, to be hundreds of millions in annual revenue once ramped. Qualification with the hyperscaler is targeted by mid-2027, with commercial deployments by late-2027 to early-2028.

Aeva expanded its optical connectivity product portfolio and started commercial negotiations with a second optical customer. Management said that program could reach multiple millions of units annually starting by 2028.
Aeva signed a supply agreement to integrate the Eve sensor into Micro Epsilon's factory automation sensing solutions, a multi-thousand sensor order.

In automotive, Aeva increased shipments of production-intent Atlas sensors to Daimler Truck and passed a VDA audit for its top 10 European passenger OEM. SOPs and ramps for both programs begin in 2027-29. The Daimler order book is about $1 bn over the program life and the top 10 OEM program could be at least as large.

Aeva completed an ADAS development program with Bendix and is now in commercial negotiations. It was also selected by the US Air Force and US Navy for joint development of 4D lidar for remote sensing and airborne autonomy.
There was no update to 2026 guidance, but the company said it is tracking well for the year. Prior guidance was $30.0 mn to $36.0 mn revenue, against GS at $32.6 mn and the Street at $31.6 mn.

GS keeps a Neutral rating and cuts its 12-month price target to $11 from $15 on lower peer-comp multiples. GS sees momentum as largely reflected in Street estimates and valuation, with execution and market risk remaining.

market_movers.rationale: GS cut its price target to $11 from $15 on lower peer multiples (4X EV/2028 sales versus 5X) while keeping Neutral. It sees momentum as largely priced into Street estimates and valuation.

earnings_insights: AEVA 3Q26 (reported 11/4): revenue $6.7 mn actual versus GS estimate $6.5 mn and FactSet Street estimate $6.6 mn, up 86.3% y/y.
AEVA 3Q26 (reported 11/4): adjusted EBIT ex-SBC -$27.7 mn actual versus GS estimate -$26.6 mn and Street estimate -$33.4 mn. Adjusted EBIT including SBC was -$39.1 mn versus GS estimate -$35.3 mn.
AEVA 3Q26 (reported 11/4): non-GAAP EPS ex-SBC -$0.39 actual versus GS estimate -$0.39 and Street estimate -$0.43. GS estimates non-GAAP EPS including SBC at -$0.56 versus GS estimate -$0.51.
AEVA FY2026 revenue guidance of $30.0 mn to $36.0 mn was not updated. GS estimates $32.6 mn and the Street (FactSet) $31.6 mn.
GS EPS estimates including SBC moved to -$2.19 (CY26), -$2.10 (CY27) and -$1.50 (CY28) from -$2.10, -$1.95 and -$1.35 on higher opex and SBC. Excluding SBC they are now -$1.58, -$1.45 and -$0.85.
GS revenue estimates are unchanged at $32.6 mn (CY26E), $68.0 mn (CY27E) and $215.0 mn (CY28E).
risk_factors: Ability to win new business: more or fewer production awards in autos and non-autos, including datacenter, than GS expects could drive upside or downside.
ASPs: revenue per lidar above or below GS expectations would change revenue and the stock.
Trade policy: third-party manufacturers Jabil and Fabrinet produce in Mexico and APAC, and adverse trade decisions could raise costs.
Input costs: higher or lower prices for metals, semis and other components could drive downside or upside.
Execution and market risk remain, per GS.
geopolitical: Aeva's 4D lidar was selected for joint development by the US Air Force and US Navy for remote sensing and airborne autonomy, its first air-based A&D award.
GS lists trade policy as a risk because Aeva uses third-party manufacturers Jabil and Fabrinet, which produce globally including Mexico and APAC.
